subject: POC follow-up: recommended model shortlist, benchmarks and next actions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finsight.ai>, Tom Kramer <tom.kramer@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC follow-up: recommended model shortlist, benchmarks and next actions

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Great to see the ingestion pipeline and the end-user retrieval flows; the sample query set exposed a few ranking edge cases we should cover during the POC. Per our conversation, I captured a recommended shortlist and the immediate asks for the trial so we can hit the 2-week evaluation window you requested.

Key recommended shortlist (tradeoffs at a glance):
- Redwood-7B-int8 (default reco) — best latency and cost for real-time UI (avg token latency ~45ms), good quality on short prompts, lower cost per 1k tokens. Worth starting here for a baseline.
- LlamaX-13B-4bit — balanced option: higher quality for multi-sentence summarization and reranking tasks, moderate latency (~120ms) when pinned to dedicated capacity. Slightly higher cost but fewer hallucinations on our tests.
- Falcon-40B-s2 (quantized) — quality leader on long-context QA and extraction; higher CPU/GPU memory needs and cost. Recommend only for batch-heavy or server-side enrichment flows.

Why these three: they cover the latency/cost/quality space you described — Redwood-7B-int8 for UI interactivity, LlamaX-13B-4bit for middle-ground quality, Falcon-40B-s2 for accuracy-sensitive backfill or nightly jobs.

Included in the attached benchmark_summary_20271017.pdf and the Drive folder linked below are per-model: latency distributions (p50/p95), token cost estimates at your expected traffic (~600k tokens/day), and prompt-set performance on your sample queries. Also attached is a starting prompt set (finsight_prompt_set_v1.csv) we used for scoring.

Immediate asks / MAP suggestions:
1) Provide a 48-hour access snapshot to a representative query sample (anonymized) — finSight to drop in the shared Drive folder.
2) Redwood to run the three-model baseline against your sample and return: p50/p95 latency, F1/exact-match for extraction prompts, and hallucination rate estimate. (We’ll use your metric thresholds; if none, we’ll propose defaults.)
3) Agree on the evaluation success criteria and a go/no-go date (suggested: 2027-11-01).
4) Pricing note: we’ll propose a short-term trial credit package and a conversion estimate after baseline — Ben/team to share by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: finsight_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt id, intent, expected output), benchmark_summary_20271017.pdf, mutual_action_plan_FS-2027-0429.xlsx

Next steps: Elena / Tom can you confirm who will upload the anonymized sample and whether the 11/01 go/no-go works?

Thanks — happy to run the baseline as soon as we have the sample.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finsight.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Kramer <tom.kramer@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: recommended model shortlist, benchmarks and next actions

Thanks Ben — that looks good.

We’ll upload a 48-hour anonymized query dump by tomorrow morning to the Drive folder (I’ll drop it under /FinSight/Samples/PII-scrubbed). 11/01 as a go/no-go works for us.

A couple of follow-ups from our side before you run the baseline:
- Can you include hallucination checks for entity extraction (we see this frequently with longer context docs).
- We need rough $/1k token estimates for each model variant so we can budget (baseline and projected at 1M tokens/day).
- Also please attach the prompt-set mapping to user intent (helps our product team prioritize tests).

Tom — looping you to confirm whether we want Falcon-40B only for batch pipelines or also for prioritized server-side calls.

Appreciate the speedy turnaround.

—
Elena Ortiz
Head of Product | FinSight
elena.ortiz@finsight.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: recommended model shortlist, benchmarks and next actions

Ben / Marissa — quick internal note (cc’d so it’s in-thread):

Agree with the three-model breadth. A couple of operational guardrails we should include in the baseline run so FinSight can make an apples-to-apples decision:
- Evaluate at two sequence-length buckets: short UI (<=256 tokens) and long-doc (2048 tokens) to show latency/cost inflection points.
- Provide per-model quantization profile we’ll run (int8 vs 4-bit) and the exact execution config (batch sizes, KV cache size) used for the reported numbers.
- Add a simple regression-check harness: run a fixed set of 50 golden prompts and compute exact-match drop vs. Redwood-7B-int8 baseline; flag any >6% drop as a quality regression.

If Marissa can own the baseline run and the regression report, I’ll draft the suggested MAP timeline and trial credit note for pricing.

—Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finsight.ai>, Tom Kramer <tom.kramer@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: recommended model shortlist, benchmarks and next actions

On Mon, Oct 18, 2027 at 10:05 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Key recommended shortlist (tradeoffs at a glance):
> - Redwood-7B-int8 (default reco) — best latency and cost for real-time UI (avg token latency ~45ms), good quality on short prompts, lower cost per 1k tokens.
> - LlamaX-13B-4bit — balanced option: higher quality for multi-sentence summarization and reranking tasks, moderate latency (~120ms) when pinned to dedicated capacity.
> - Falcon-40B-s2 (quantized) — quality leader on long-context QA and extraction; higher CPU/GPU memory needs and cost.

Thanks — I’ll run the baseline per Karthik’s buckets and include the regression harness. Delivery plan:
- Today/Tomorrow: confirm exact dataset location and schema (Elena to upload).
- 48 hours after data receipt: baseline run (p50/p95 latency, cost calc at 600k & 1M tokens/day).
- 72 hours after run: full regression report + prompt-level failure cases and short list of mitigations.

I’ve attached (in-thread) the initial prompt mapping (finsight_prompt_set_v1.csv) and will upload the full run artifacts to the Drive folder.

Questions for FinSight: do you have a preferred threshold for the regression flag (Karthik suggested 6%) or should we use your internal acceptance criteria? Also, any additional compliance checks (e.g., redaction verification) we should run on the sample?

—
Marissa Cole
Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finsight.ai>, Tom Kramer <tom.kramer@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: POC follow-up: recommended model shortlist, benchmarks and next actions

Elena / Tom — great, appreciate the quick coordination.

To confirm next actions:
- FinSight to upload anonymized 48-hour query sample to Drive by tomorrow morning.
- Marissa to run baseline across the three models and two length buckets within 48 hours of upload.
- Karthik to prepare MAP and a trial credit note; Ben to send the $/1k token card for each model by COB tomorrow.
- Go/no-go target: 2027-11-01.

If FinSight prefers Falcon-40B only for batch, we’ll mark the model as optional for server-side calls in the MAP. If you want to test it for prioritized server-side enrichment, please flag that in the Drive upload (we’ll account for higher resource requirements in the cost estimate).

Attached: mutual_action_plan_FS-2027-0429.xlsx (starter MAP that includes timeline, responsibilities, and success criteria).

We’ll kick off as soon as the sample lands.

Thanks —
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

summary: Post-demo POC follow-up: Ben proposed a three-model shortlist (Redwood-7B-int8, LlamaX-13B-4bit, Falcon-40B-s2) covering latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. FinSight will upload anonymized sample; Redwood team (Marissa, Karthik, Ben) to run baseline across two length buckets and produce latency/cost/regression reports. Mutual action plan and pricing card to be delivered prior to 11/01 go/no-go.
